# llms-full.txt

## Project summary

StealthEye Agent OS is a foundation for broad delegated autonomy: authorized online-task agents operating through ChatGPT custom apps/MCP, durable workers, Mission OS, app-host surfaces, mission-scoped authority, signed manifests, Guard decisions, evals, receipts, replayable evidence, and compliance-ready controls. This public repo contains non-sensitive architecture, specs, governance, scaffolding, eval templates, and compliance planning only.

## Current build state

Build 2 adds `@stealtheye/agent-registry`: signed agent/tool manifests, JSON Schema export, deterministic canonicalization, SHA-256 digesting, Ed25519 signing/verification helpers, risk-relevant diffing, in-memory trust registry, revocation lists, public fixtures, and Vitest eval-style cases.

Build 3 adds `@stealtheye/guard`: capability-token schemas, requested actions, Guard decisions/receipts, lifecycle helpers, deterministic token/action matching, hard-stop evaluation, registry trust checks, public fixtures, and Vitest eval-style cases.

Build 4 adds `@stealtheye/mission-os`: StealthEye Mission Language, normalized mission schemas, authority envelopes, lightweight mission plans, status snapshots, receipt references, compiler outputs for Guard capability-token templates and requested actions, public fixtures, and Vitest eval-style cases.

Build 5 adds `@stealtheye/app-host`: app metadata, MCP-style preview tool descriptors, input/output schemas, resource descriptors, fixture-backed handlers, and Vitest eval-style tests for host, mission, Guard, registry, and policy tool families. All Build 5 tools are read-only, fixture-only, or preview-only.

Build 6 adds `@stealtheye/worker-fleet`: typed worker task schemas, task types/statuses, lease schemas with fencing tokens, idempotency records and stable action fingerprints, retry policy/state helpers, task status summaries, artifact references, worker receipt events, Guard preflight helpers, Mission OS plan-to-worker-task conversion, fixtures, and Vitest eval-style tests.

## Architecture overview

The default stack is TypeScript monorepo, Node.js MCP servers, Postgres for durable mission/control/evidence state, Redis + BullMQ for initial worker queues, Temporal as future workflow orchestration, S3/R2-compatible artifact storage, GitHub App auth, Playwright BrowserOps, OpenAI Responses API + Apps SDK integration, and Zod + JSON Schema for mission/tool/workflow/receipt/authority/agent-card/worker schemas.

Key systems: Mission OS, App Host, Agent Registry, Guard, Capability Tokens, Worker Fleet, CodeOps, CI Repair, BrowserOps, Receipts + Replay, Memory Graph, Evals, Workflow Compiler, Semantic Firewall, A2A Subagent Network, Agent Arena, StagingOps/Observability, and domain ops apps.

## App Host model

App Host is the first ChatGPT App / MCP Server Host Shell foundation. It models tool/resource descriptors and fixture-backed handlers that can later be wired to an official MCP or ChatGPT Apps runtime. Build 5 does not expose live repo mutation, worker execution, browser automation, deployments, money movement, customer data, remote trust discovery, or production-grade credential flows.

## Mission OS model

Mission OS converts broad goals into typed Mission Language, normalized mission objects, authority envelopes, plan/DAG structures, status summaries, receipt references, and Guard-compatible requested actions. Build 6 Worker Fleet consumes Mission OS plans and preserves mission, plan, step, dependency, receipt, capability-token, and requested-action context when creating worker tasks.

## Worker Fleet model

Worker Fleet is the durable execution substrate contract for future mission-step execution. Build 6 defines package-level schemas and deterministic helpers for worker tasks, leases, idempotency, retries, status transitions, summaries, artifacts, receipts, Guard preflight, and Mission OS handoff.

Build 6 intentionally does not add a live Redis/BullMQ queue, production worker runtime, distributed locking service, live tool execution, repo mutation, browser automation, production deployment, customer-data workflows, money movement, live queue configuration, or real artifact storage.

## Agent Registry and Guard model

Signed payloads are verified over canonical unsigned payloads. Guard consumes registry trust summaries and enforces capability-token constraints, pinned digests, hard stops, lifecycle state, and mission-scoped target/effect boundaries.

Capability tokens are delegated-authority records. Authority envelopes produced by Mission OS are templates/structures that can later feed Guard-capability issuance. Worker Fleet calls Guard preflight for action-bearing tasks and records receipt/status suggestions without executing actions.

## Mission/build workflow

1. Jamie opens a new ChatGPT tab for the next build prompt.
2. Builder completes focused repo work on a branch.
3. Builder updates docs, AGENTS.md, llms files, eval expectations, receipt/evidence expectations, and verification checklist where applicable.
4. Jamie returns to verifier chat with PR/branch/commit.
5. Verifier checks implementation against issue #1 and docs.
6. Verifier updates issue #1.
7. Verifier provides the next prompt.

## Docs map

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: system components and data/control flow.
- `docs/AUTONOMY_MODEL.md`: authority, autonomy, and hard stops.
- `docs/WORKER_FLEET.md`: Build 6 task, lease, idempotency, retry, receipt, artifact, Guard preflight, and Mission OS handoff contracts.
- `docs/APP_HOST.md`: Build 5 app-host tool/resource surface and boundaries.
- `docs/MISSION_OS.md`: Mission Language, mission schemas, compiler, status, receipts, Guard integration, and Worker Fleet handoff.
- `docs/CUSTOM_APPS.md`: app inventory and responsibilities.
- `docs/AGENT_REGISTRY.md`: signed cards/manifests, trust, revocation, Guard integration assumptions.
- `docs/SECURITY.md`: MCP/OAuth/security boundaries, Worker Fleet no-runtime boundary, and hard stops.
- `docs/WORKFLOWS.md`: mission lifecycle, worker handoff, DAGs, retries, idempotency.
- `docs/EVALS.md`: eval philosophy and suites.
- `docs/RECEIPTS.md` and `docs/EVIDENCE_MODEL.md`: evidence and replay.
- Compliance/security/governance docs map controls to readiness, not certification.

## Compliance and evidence summary

The project intends to align evidence with NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act readiness, ISO/IEC 42001 readiness, NIST CSF 2.0, NIST SSDF, OWASP LLM/Agentic threats, SOC 2 readiness, ISO 27001/27002/27701 readiness, GDPR/CCPA readiness, SLSA/SBOM/provenance, and sector-triggered frameworks. No certification is claimed.

## Public/private boundary

Public: architecture, public specs, non-sensitive schemas, app/tool scaffolding, worker-fleet contracts, examples/mock data, eval templates, governance and compliance docs. Private: sensitive operational material, production infrastructure, customer data, deployed runtime configuration, and internal accounts.

## Verification commands

```bash
pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
```
